title: Letter 22 — The Second Coming
attribution_note: Letter 22 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: Herewith I send thee also concerning the Second Coming of Christ, of which we spoke briefly when thou wast with me; and I counsel thee to walk according to what is written.

Christians — and especially in this present last time, when from the first coming of Christ already more than one thousand seven hundred and eighty years are past — in this present time, I say, those who live must every day expect the Second Coming of Christ, and prepare themselves for it by worthy repentance.

When an earthly king is minded to come into some city, and the city knoweth of it, all its citizens expect him and prepare themselves to meet him and receive him. The Heavenly King, Jesus Christ, is minded to come again, of which He Himself, while He lived upon the earth, declared, and His servants the holy apostles have preached unto us, and the holy Church looketh for it. Therefore must Christians, as those who know of this His coming, prepare themselves to meet Him and receive Him, and expect Him every day — because He shall come unexpected; and the more so, that He shall come not as He came the first time, in humility and poverty, but shall come in terrible glory. He shall come not to live upon the earth, to teach and to suffer (that hath already been), but to judge and to render to every man according to his works.

sections.heading: Be ready, for ye know not the hour

pairs.en: If an angel from heaven came unto us and said, “Behold, in these days shall be the coming of Christ” — how would all tremble, and turn to true repentance! Every man would keep himself from sin, and with sighing and tears would propitiate God, and the rest. But who knoweth how long yet the coming of Christ shall tarry? It may be even in these days. For no man knoweth the counsel of God and His decree. For it is said: *“Be ye also ready: for in such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh”* [Matthew 24:44].

As of the first coming of Christ the prophets preached, saying, “Christ shall come, Christ shall come into the world” — and Christ came when the time appointed for Him was come — so also of the Second Coming the teachers of the Church preach and say: “Christ shall come to judge the quick and the dead; He shall come to judge, and shall appear unexpected, as lightning.” In what fear and despair shall sinners then be, who now think not upon that dreadful day, and prepare not themselves for it by true repentance!

sections.heading: The day of the Lord is at hand

pairs.en: Therefore let us think, beloved, every day, and let us prepare ourselves for the meeting of our Lord: for the day of the Lord is already nigh, and unexpected, as lightning, shall it shine forth. I know that the apostle wrote unto the Thessalonians, saying: *“That ye be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand”* [2 Thessalonians 2:2]. But from that time already more than one thousand seven hundred and eighty years are past, as is said above. Therefore we, after so many years gone by, must look for it shortly, and with the apostle James confess: *“the coming of the Lord draweth nigh; behold, the judge standeth before the door”* [James 5:8–9] — and the more so, when we already see that *“because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold”* [Matthew 24:12], and piety is trampled under foot, and ungodliness multiplieth more and more; the word of God is despised, and almost every man is given over to vanity alone, and few seek the salvation of the soul with a sincere heart. What, then, in such circumstances, is to be looked for, save that unexpected we shall hear the cry: *“Behold, the bridegroom cometh; go ye out to meet him”* [Matthew 25:6]?

sections.heading: The evil servant and the mockers

pairs.en: Therefore take heed, beloved, that thou say not in thine heart, and do not that which is written of the evil servant: *“But and if that evil servant shall say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming; and shall begin to smite his fellowservants, and to eat and drink with the drunken; the lord of that servant shall come in a day when he looketh not for him, and in an hour that he is not aware of, and shall cut him asunder, and appoint him his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth”* [Matthew 24:48–51] — lest thou also suffer in like manner. And withdraw thyself from the scoffers described by holy Peter, which say: *“Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation.”* *“The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness”* [2 Peter 3:4, 9]. *“For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them”* [1 Thessalonians 5:3]. But let us, according to the Lord's exhortation, *“Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning; and ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding; that when he cometh and knocketh, they may open unto him immediately.* *Blessed are those servants, whom the lord when he cometh shall find watching”* [Luke 12:35–37].

Let us write upon the heart the word of our Lord: *“Be ye also ready: for in such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh,”* who saith: *“Behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be”* [Revelation 22:12]. Faithful is the word of God, and it can in no wise lie. He cometh, He cometh to judge, the Lord; He cometh quickly, and shall come then when men look not for Him, and His reward is with Him, to give every man according as his work shall be.

And the more time multiplieth from His first coming, the nearer is the second coming unto us; and the longer we live, the nearer we draw unto His universal Judgment; and today we are already nearer to that day and hour than we were yesterday and the day before. Let us write this in our memory, and by true repentance prepare ourselves. *“Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering;* *(for he is faithful that promised;) and let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching”* [Hebrews 10:23–25].

sections.heading: Repent, that that day may be consolation

pairs.en: Therefore let us repent, beloved, that consolation, and not fear and horror and despair, may that dreadful day bring unto us sinners. *“God... now commandeth all men every where to repent: because he hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness”* [Acts 17:30–31]. From this followeth such consolation: Christ the Lord shall judge the world; therefore God commandeth all men to repent, that they may escape that dreadful sentence of condemnation: *“Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels.”*

Let us turn, then, beloved, with all the heart unto God. Let us repent, and He will forgive us our sins, and we shall escape condemnation, and the Judgment of Christ shall give us not fear and trembling, but consolation and eternal salvation. For Christ the Lord shall judge not them that have sinned, but them that have sinned and not repented; but them that have sinned and repented He will have mercy and save. For to this end also He came into the world, that He might save them that have sinned and repented — which I wish for myself and for thee.
